headline: One Dad's Library Trips Sparked a Brotherhood Movement
meta_description: Khari Arnold's weekly library visits with his daughter inspired Library Dads, a free community event where fathers bond over books and model engagement.
summary_short: When Khari Arnold took his infant daughter to the Atlanta library, he didn't expect to launch a movement. Now dozens of dads gather regularly to bond through books.
body:
What began as a personal ritual between a Georgia father and his infant daughter has blossomed into a cherished community gathering that sends a powerful message: dads show up. Khari Arnold started taking his daughter Ariah to the library when she was just four months old, discovering that their weekly outings became far more than routine—they strengthened their relationship and sparked early literacy development in his child. Recognizing that other fathers might crave similar connection, Arnold opened the doors to his weekly tradition, inviting dads throughout Atlanta to bring children of any age. Today, Library Dads events fill up quickly, drawing fathers hungry for both camaraderie and purpose. The gatherings remain free, making them accessible to families across the community.

For participants like Derrick Lampkin, who brings his sons Dominique and Tristan—and more recently his seven-month-old daughter Madeleine Sophia—the impact extends beyond the books themselves. "We continue coming because it shows my boys that dads show up," Lampkin explained, underscoring why these library visits matter. Similarly, Kassell Scott, father to three-year-old Amahle, found the gatherings eye-opening and motivating, discovering other engaged fathers in his community.

The simple alliteration carries weight: bonding through books, building brotherhood. In a culture where paternal presence often goes unexamined, Library Dads has created a visible, recurring space where fathers normalize their involvement in their children's lives and learning. Arnold's instinct to transform a personal moment into a shared community practice has given dozens of Atlanta dads—and their children—something increasingly rare: a regular gathering where showing up is the whole point.
quick_facts: Khari Arnold founded Library Dads after weekly visits with his four-month-old daughter Ariah
Based in Atlanta, Georgia; events are free and fill up quickly
Fathers bring children of any age; participants include Derrick Lampkin and Kassell Scott
Focus: bonding through books and building brotherhood among engaged fathers
